title: Accuracy and latency trade-offs
task_statement: Meet a latency target and an accuracy floor by setting model, effort, and delivery mode with measured receipts. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Model and effort choice for latency
components.first_principle: Latency rises with model size, output length, and effort, so choose the smallest model and effort that pass the quality target.

nodes.label: Model and effort chosen per task
Larger Claude model at higher effort
p95 latency and quality score per stage

steps: Engineer a prompt that works well first, then measure baseline latency and time to first token.
Choose the smallest model that meets the quality target on your test set.
Set output_config effort to a lower level for simple tasks.
Set max_tokens to a value that the expected output fits.
Ask for a shorter answer in the prompt when output length adds time.
Move hard tasks to a larger model only when the measured quality gap justifies the time. (Inference)
pros: The docs name Haiku 5.5 as the fastest option that keeps high intelligence.
Lower effort cuts output tokens and cost.
Fast mode raises output speed on supported Opus models without a change in intelligence.
cons: Lower effort reduces capability on hard tasks.
Fast mode uses premium pricing on every token.
Fast mode speed benefits do not target time to first token.
use_when: A user waits on an interactive answer with a fixed latency target.
Tasks are short and repeat often.
The quality test passes at a lower effort level.
do_not_use_when: The prompt is not yet tuned, because the docs say to reach good quality first.
The fast mode request targets Claude Haiku 5.5, which fast mode does not support.
The task needs the highest capability and a loose latency target.

constraints.combination: Raise effort to medium for calls that fail the quality check.

constraints.combination: Keep high effort for calls where a wrong answer is costly.

components.exam_tie: D3.3. Expect a scenario with a latency target, an accuracy floor, and a proposal to add a stage or a bigger model. The credited answer measures each stage and cuts the weakest one. (Inference)
components.trap: A bigger model looks like the accuracy fix. It adds time per call and can break the latency target.
components.decision_rule: Pick the smallest model and effort level that passes the measured quality target and the latency target.
components.exam_tip: When the scenario states a latency limit, reject an option that adds a slower step before you measure it.

components.name: Streaming for perceived latency
components.first_principle: Streaming sends output as the model generates it, so users see the first tokens before the full response ends.

nodes.label: Time to first token and total time

steps: Set stream to true on the Messages request.
The API sends server-sent events as the model generates output.
Your app renders each text delta as soon as it arrives.
Measure time to first token and total time as two separate values.
Handle streaming refusals in the client before you show the output.
pros: Users see output early, which improves perceived responsiveness.
The same request works for text, tool use, and thinking deltas.
Long requests avoid the timeout risk of one long response.
cons: The client must handle partial output and mid-stream errors.
Streaming does not reduce the model work or the token count.
Code that reads the full text runs only after the stream ends.
use_when: A person reads a chat answer as it appears.
Responses are long and the first sentence matters most.
A request could run past the requests without streaming timeout.
do_not_use_when: A batch job reads only the final object.
A downstream system needs the full response before it starts.
The client cannot process incremental events.

components.name: Batch processing and service tiers for throughput
components.first_principle: Work that can wait trades response time for half the standard price, and the batch runs in the background.

nodes.label: Your app builds one request per item

steps: Build one request for each item and give each request a custom_id.
Submit the list of requests to the Message Batches API.
Poll the batch until processing_status reads ended.
Read the results when processing ends or after 24 hours, whichever comes first.
Download the results within 29 days of creation.
Match each result to its input with the custom_id.
pros: Batch usage is charged at 50 percent of standard API prices.
One batch holds up to 100,000 requests or 256 MB.
Batch runs outside normal capacity, as the service tiers page states.
cons: Results can take up to 24 hours.
A batch can exceed the workspace spend limit slightly.
Batch is not an option for a user who waits for a reply.
use_when: An evaluation run or document backfill can wait a day.
Throughput and cost matter more than the first response time.
Many requests share a long prefix that the cache can reuse.
do_not_use_when: A user waits for a reply in a chat window.
The platform is Microsoft Foundry, Bedrock, or Google managed, where the Message Batches API is not supported.
A single request has a latency target of seconds.

components.exam_tie: D3.3. Expect a scenario with a large offline set and a throughput or cost goal. The credited answer moves that work to Batch and keeps interactive calls elsewhere. (Inference)
components.trap: Batch looks like a speed fix for a large job. Results can take up to 24 hours, so it does not meet a seconds-level target.
components.decision_rule: Use Batch when the caller accepts results within 24 hours and needs half the standard price.
components.exam_tip: If the scenario needs an answer in seconds, reject Batch whatever the volume.

flowchart TD
  A{Does a person wait for this answer?} -->|Yes| B{Is the target under a few seconds?}
  A -->|No| C{Can results arrive within 24 hours?}
  B -->|Yes| D[Haiku 5.5 at low effort with streaming]
  B -->|No| E[Smallest model that passes the quality test]
  C -->|Yes| F[Message Batches API at half price]
  C -->|No| G[Standard calls with measured stages]
  D --> H{Quality check passes?}
  E --> H
  H -->|No| I[Raise effort one level]
  H -->|Yes| J[Keep and monitor p95]

  M[Smallest model that passes quality] --> E[Lowest effort that passes quality]

  L --> X[Cut weakest receipt]
